q: Which of the following is not part of the GFA?
n: The NBC excludes mechanical penthouses, bulkheads and equipment spaces on the roof from the gross floor area. Lobbies, exits and corridors are included. Source: 2004 Revised IRR of PD 1096 (NBCP), Rule VII, Sec. 707 (Definition of GFA).

q: What is the ISA?
n: The impervious surface area is the paved surface in the open yard. That is two 3 m driveways across the 3 m front yard (18 sqm) plus the 2 m x 3 m pathway (6 sqm), or 24 sqm. Source: 2004 Revised IRR of PD 1096 (NBCP), Rule VIII, Sec. 804 and Table VIII.3 (ISA and USA).

DESIGN PROBLEM NO. 3 – SEVEN-STOREY APARTMENT BUILDING

Design Problem. A businessman-architect entered a joint venture with a landowner in Quezon City. They agreed to build an apartment building to be rented out in one of the busy commercial areas in the city. The architect will also supervise the construction of the project. The apartment building will have seven storeys and a total of 48 rentable units. The profit of the joint venture will be shared by the two. The property management once the project is completed will be handled by the landowner. After several meetings between the two parties, the following space requirements were determined:
a. The ground floor spaces are a combination of a covered parking space and the entrance facility.
i. The parking space shall accommodate 20 car parking units and an ample space for motor parking. Vehicular exit and entry shall be through two 3m driveways positioned 3m away from both front corners of the lot. This configuration allows for a one-way vehicular flow in the parking space.
ii. Tenants and visitors shall enter the building through a central pathway with a width of 2m. This short pathway (3m long) shall lead to the entrance facility of the building.
iii. The entrance facility is a group of spaces including an entrance lobby, security room, small admin room, stairs and a small passenger elevator going to the floors above. The total space for the facility is 11m wide by 5m.
iv. A utility room shall be located at the back of the parking space. The room shall measure 2.5m x 5m.
b. The 2nd to 7th floor shall be of typical layout with 8 rentable units and a common space.
i. There shall be 2 units of 2-bedroom units on both sides of the common area per floor. These units measure 7m by 81.55 sqm including a 1.8m-deep balcony facing the road.
ii. The common area is located at the front end of the 13.6m long corridor. It shall measure 58.25sqm. This area also contains the stairs and elevator leading to the ground floor.
iii. At the back of the typical floor layout are the exit, ventilation and utility rooms. These areas are connected to the back end of the long corridor.
iv. Along the sides of the 1.75m wide corridor are the 6 other units for rent (3 units on each side). There shall be 2 studio units on each side of the corridor measuring 3.4m x 8.625m including a balcony. There should also be a 1 BR unit on each side which measures 6.8m x 58.65 sqm. This area also includes the balcony.
c. The rooftop of the building shall be a flat roof with surrounding parapet measuring 513 sqm in total area. It shall be used for utility provisions such as water tanks. Bulkheads are also provided for exit and for mechanical components of the building. It can also be used for other activities of the tenants.
Site Features. The project lot is a regular rectangular lot having an area of 736 sqm and a frontage of 23m. The slope is relatively flat and currently used as an open lot for paid parking. The zone of the area is R-3 and as seen from the surrounding buildings, the front setback is 3m from the front property line. The building shall be surrounded by the minimum setbacks to maximize the profitability of the lot. The remaining open spaces around the building aside from the paved driveways and pathways shall be vegetated.
Design Objectives. The challenge for the architect of the project is the flexibility of the units. There shall be enough space for different space configurations catering different lifestyles of the tenants. The common area shall be used for socialization and shall be designed to engage the tenants in meaningful encounters with its neighbors. Aside from flexibility and socialization, another challenge shall be the marketability of the units.

q: What is the minimum fire rating for occupancy separation walls?
n: Occupancy separations are rated from 1 to 4 hours depending on the occupancies. The minimum is 1 hour. Source: RA 9514 (Fire Code) 2019 RIRR (Separation of Occupancies); 2004 Revised IRR of PD 1096 (NBCP), Rule VII.

q: If a commercial space shall be added to the project, what should be the maximum proportion of commercial space for it to be considered as a minor accessory occupancy?
n: A mixed use may be treated as a minor accessory occupancy when it takes up no more than 10% of the floor area of the story or building. Source: NFPA 101, Sec. 6.1.14.1.3 (Accessory Occupancies); RA 9514 RIRR.

q: According to the building code, who can be construction inspectors?
n: Per the exam key, inspections of building works are carried out by licensed professionals, chiefly architects and civil engineers, under the Building Official's supervision. Source: PD 1096 (NBCP), Sec. 207 (Duties of a Building Official) and the 2004 Revised IRR, Rule II.

q: A pencil test is used to measure the hardness of what?
n: The pencil hardness test scratches a coating with pencils of graded hardness (6B to 9H) to rate the film's hardness. Source: ASTM D3363 (Film Hardness by Pencil Test).

q: What millwork is used to cover the gap between the floor and wall?
n: A baseboard (skirting) is the millwork strip at the foot of a wall. It covers the gap between floor and wall and protects the wall finish. Source: Ching, A Visual Dictionary of Architecture; Ching, Building Construction Illustrated, Ch. 10.

q: The most durable paint sheen.
n: The higher the sheen, the harder and more washable the film. Gloss is the most durable sheen. Source: Master Painters Institute (MPI) Gloss and Sheen Standards.

q: What is the minimum head clearance for a mezzanine floor?
n: The NBC requires mezzanine floors to have at least 1.80 m clear headroom above and below. Source: 2004 Revised IRR of PD 1096 (NBCP), Rule VIII (Mezzanine Floors).

q: What fitting is used for point-supported curtain walls?
n: A point-supported glass system creates a flexible and modular wall that can be used in large spaces to create smaller areas for specific purposes from conference rooms to showrooms. They are also a high wall system designed to work well in large open areas. If you search how this system looks like, you will see that it usually uses spider fittings. Point-supported glass curtain walls are held at bolted points by spider fittings with articulated bolts. Source: GANA Glazing Manual (Point-Supported Glass Systems).

q: What is the ideal construction for an accessible shower?
n: A roll-in shower has no curb or step, so a wheelchair user can roll straight in. Source: BP 344 2024 Revised IRR (Accessible Showers); ADA Standards, Sec. 608.2.2.

q: In construction, a preamble can be seen where?
n: A preamble is a short explanation of the contract usually, but not always, found on the document's first page. It typically includes: Name and address of the project. Name and address of the project owner. Name of the design professional, if applicable. A preamble is the introductory part of a contract, stating the parties, background and purpose before the operative clauses. Source: Civil Code of the Philippines (contracts); UAP SPP Doc. 202 (contract forms).

q: What type of kitchen layout can best benefit from using an air admittance valve?
n: An island sink cannot easily be vented through a wall. An air admittance valve lets air into the drain to protect the trap seal without a conventional vent pipe. Source: International Plumbing Code, Sec. 918 (Air Admittance Valves); Revised National Plumbing Code.

q: What is the ideal placement of wall sconces in a bathroom?
n: Sconces on both sides of the mirror, at about face height, light the face evenly without shadows. Source: IES Lighting Handbook (Residential Lighting – Grooming); Ching, Interior Design Illustrated.

q: What are the two types of filing cabinets?
n: Per the exam key, filing cabinets come as pedestal units (under-desk, mobile) and lateral cabinets (wide, side-opening drawers). Vertical cabinets are the other common type. Source: Time-Saver Standards for Interior Design (Office Furniture); BIFMA X5.9 (Storage Units).

q: What is the TGFA of the project?
n: The overall covered area on the ground floor is 513sqm. The 2F to 7F typical floor area is also 513sqm. The rooftop area is also 513sqm. Therefore, the TGFA of the project is 513sqm x 8 = 4,104 sqm. Per the exam key, the 513 sqm floor area repeats over seven storeys plus the roof deck. Source: 2004 Revised IRR of PD 1096 (NBCP), Rule VII, Sec. 707 (TGFA).

q: What is the approximate area of the vegetated OSL?
n: The lot is 736 sqm (23 m x 32 m) and the footprint is 513 sqm, leaving 223 sqm of open space. Subtract the 24 sqm of paved driveways and pathway: about 199 sqm is vegetated. Source: 2004 Revised IRR of PD 1096 (NBCP), Rule VIII, Sec. 804 (Unpaved Surface Area).

q: If the project is to be fully maximized with firewalls on both sides, what is the total firewall length allowed by the code?
n: There are two conditions that should be followed for 2-sides firewalls in R-3 developments. The maximum length of the firewalls shall be: 85% of each side property line - 27.2m at each side (54.4m for both sides) 65% of the total perimeter - 71.5m total Therefore, the 54.4m total firewall length shall prevail since it is the least. With firewalls on two sides, the smaller of the two limits governs, so 54.4 m. Source: 2004 Revised IRR of PD 1096 (NBCP), Rule VII, Sec. 708 (Firewalls) and Table VII.4.

q: If additional off-site parking is required for the project, what should be the distance of the parking site from the building?
n: Per the exam key, additional parking should be at most 10 m from the building. Code note: the NBC allows off-site parking up to 200 m from the building it serves. Source: 2004 Revised IRR of PD 1096 (NBCP), Rule VII, Sec. 707 (off-site parking).

q: A ledge to be used for the outdoor unit of each unit’s split AC shall be provided. What is the maximum extension of the ledge from the outermost face of the building?
n: Since the building footprint is maximized, the area beyond the outermost face of the building is already the yards. According to the code, the maximum projections on yards, courts and lightwells shall be 1.2m. Where the footprint reaches the setback line, AC ledges project into the yard. The NBC limits such projections to about 1.20 m from the outermost face of the building. Source: 2004 Revised IRR of PD 1096 (NBCP), Rule VII/VIII (Projections into Yards).

q: A structural element used purely for tension.
n: Cables carry loads in pure tension only. Struts work in compression, and chords and beams take combined actions. Source: Schodek & Bechthold, Structures (Cable Structures); Ching, Building Structures Illustrated.

q: A structure that experiences hoop force.
n: Domes carry meridional forces plus circumferential hoop forces: compression near the crown and tension near the base, which needs a tension ring. Source: Schodek & Bechthold, Structures (Shells and Domes).

q: What is used as a bearing material for a seismic isolator?
n: Elastomeric seismic isolators are laminated rubber bearings, often with lead cores, alternated with steel shims. They decouple the building from ground motion. Source: NSCP 2015, Sec. 208 (Seismically Isolated Structures); Naeim & Kelly, Design of Seismic Isolated Structures.

q: What is the minimum thickness of a 4-hr fire rated CHB wall?
n: A 4-hour fire-rated concrete hollow block wall needs about 200 mm (8 in) of equivalent thickness, grouted solid. Source: RA 9514 (Fire Code) 2019 RIRR (Fire Resistance of Walls); ACI 216.1 (Fire Resistance of Concrete and Masonry).

q: What is the minimum thickness of 1-hr fire rated RC column?
n: A reinforced concrete column needs a minimum dimension of about 200 mm for a 1-hour fire rating. Source: ACI 216.1, Table 4.5.1 (Minimum Column Dimensions for Fire Resistance); RA 9514 RIRR.

q: In a performance theater with proscenium layout, which type of aisle is the least desirable?
n: In a proscenium theater a single center aisle takes the best seats on the centerline. Continental seating (no center aisle) or side aisles are preferred. Source: Time-Saver Standards for Building Types (Theaters); Neufert, Architects' Data.

q: Which is not included in architectural interiors?
n: Per the exam key, architectural interiors deal with finishes, furniture and furnishings, while fittings are treated as building services and hardware. Note: item 194 is keyed differently. Source: RA 9266, Sec. 3 (Architectural Interiors); Architect's Guidelines (2016), Sec. 7.3.

q: What is the standard height of a convenience outlet from the floor?
n: Convenience outlets are commonly mounted about 300 mm above the finished floor. Source: Philippine Electrical Code (PEC) residential practice; Time-Saver Standards for Housing (Electrical Outlets).

q: Which of the following is not considered an electrical space provision for the project?
n: Electrical space provisions include the electrical room, panel board room and transformer room. A sump pit belongs to plumbing and drainage. Source: Philippine Electrical Code (PEC) Part 1, Art. 1.10 and 4.50 (Electrical Spaces); Revised National Plumbing Code.

q: What is the best method to let hot air escape in a room?
n: Hot air rises and collects under the ceiling, so a ceiling exhaust fan removes it most directly. Source: ASHRAE Handbook – HVAC Applications (Ventilation); Philippine Green Building Code (2015), Indoor Environmental Quality.

q: What is the area of the purchased lot for the project?
n: Per the exam key, the area from the technical description is about 342 sqm. Source: Brinker & Wolf, Elementary Surveying (Area by Double Meridian Distance); DENR-LMB Manual for Land Surveying.

DESIGN PROBLEM NO. 2 – TWO-STOREY DUPLEX RESIDENTIAL

Design Problem. A successful businesswoman wanted to try to venture out in the real estate industry. She recently purchased a lot from a famous developer located in a low density residential area of Mabalacat, Pampanga. Her friend, who is an architect, was commissioned to do the residential project. The architect suggested a two-storey duplex house to accommodate two families. Upon the initial and succeeding meetings, the following space requirements were determined by the architect:
a. The two units shall have the same uniform floor area. Each unit has a paved 2- car carport where a standard 3m x 5m car slot can be accommodated. A covered porch measuring 3m x 6 sqm welcomes the guests.
b. The layout of one unit is mirrored on the other. On the ground floor, there should be a foyer, stairs leading to the next floor level, toilet and bath and a bedroom - all these spaces along the party wall. The living, dining and kitchen spaces enjoy the direct view of the side yards.
c. The second floor of each unit contains two bedrooms (one is a master bedroom) each with a walk-in closet and its own T&B. The 2nd floor plate measures 91 sqm including two 6-sqm balconies connected to each bedroom. The floor slab has a 100mm thickness made of reinforced concrete.
d. Entrance steps shall be provided from the front yard to the entrance porch.
Site Features. The purchased lot is fronting a road on one of its sides. The road runs exactly along the N-S axis. The lot parcel is bounded on the W along line 1-2 by Lot 5; on the N along line 2-3 by a community garden maintained by HOA; on the E along line 3-4 by a public RROW; and on the S along line 4-1 by Lot 7. Looking at the land title of the lot, its technical description reads from point 1; N 6°20' E, 18m to point 2; S 83°40' E, 18m to point 3; (unreadable bearings) to point 4; N 83°40' W, 20m back to point 1. The slope of the lot runs downward at 2% from North to South.
Design Objectives. The subdivision guidelines allow the use of front yards as paved carport as long as the required open space is complied. The guidelines also required lot owners to add 500mm to the minimum front setback required by the building code. All other setbacks shall follow the code. As the front lot line is oblique to the other lot lines, the front setback shall be measured from point 3 of the lot. It means that the front yard areas vary between the two units. The local zoning ordinance allows duplex structures in a low density residential zone.

q: What is the area of the paved carports?
n: Per the exam key, the two 2-car carports total about 72 sqm. Source: 2004 Revised IRR of PD 1096 (NBCP), Rule VII, Sec. 707 (Parking slot dimensions).

q: How many valleys does a simple hipped roof have?
n: A simple hipped roof on a rectangular plan has only ridges and hips, which are external angles. Valleys occur only where roofs meet at inside corners, as on L-shaped plans. Source: Ching, A Visual Dictionary of Architecture (Roof); Ching, Building Construction Illustrated, Ch. 6.

q: It is the most common type of roof.
n: The gable roof is the most common roof form. It is simple, economical, sheds water well and is easy to ventilate. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated, Ch. 6 (Roof Forms).

q: Which roof requires longer gutter length?
n: A hipped roof has eaves on all four sides, so gutters run around the whole perimeter. A gable roof needs them only on two sides. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated, Ch. 7 (Gutters); Fajardo, Simplified Construction Estimate.

q: A collar tie is installed in the ____ of the opposing gable rafters.
n: Collar ties are placed in the upper third of opposing rafters, near the ridge. They keep the rafters from spreading apart or separating at the ridge under wind uplift. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated, Ch. 6 (Rafter Framing); IRC R802.4.6.

q: What is the most common way to make a 90-degree connection of a roofing gutter?
n: A 90° gutter corner is usually made on site by notching, cutting and bending the gutter, then sealing and riveting the joint. Source: SMACNA Architectural Sheet Metal Manual (Gutters); Ching, Building Construction Illustrated, Ch. 7.

q: What is the type of roof storm drainage used for a typical gas station canopy?
n: Per the exam key, a gas-station canopy is usually drained by gutters set along valleys of the roof, routed down the columns. Source: SMACNA Architectural Sheet Metal Manual (Gutters and Downspouts); canopy manufacturers' details.

q: What is the minimum depth of a walk-in closet?
n: A walk-in closet with hanging on one side needs a minimum depth of about 1.20 m: 600 mm for clothes plus a 600 mm aisle. Source: Panero & Zelnik, Human Dimension and Interior Space (Closets); Neufert, Architects' Data.

q: What is the usual height of a bar chair?
n: Bar stools for standard bar counters (about 1,000–1,100 mm) have seats about 700–760 mm high. Source: Panero & Zelnik, Human Dimension and Interior Space (Bar Seating); Neufert, Architects' Data.

q: What is the diameter of a dressing circle when in comes to space planning?
n: Space-planning references allow a dressing circle of about 3 ft (900 mm) in diameter as the floor space a person needs to dress. Source: Panero & Zelnik, Human Dimension and Interior Space (Bedrooms – Dressing Space); Time-Saver Standards for Housing.

q: What is the usual color coding of residential zones in land use maps?
n: In land-use and zoning maps, residential zones are shown in yellow (deeper shades for higher densities). Commercial is red and industrial is violet. Source: HLURB Guidebook for CLUP Formulation (Land Use Color Codes).

q: The master bedroom occupies 40% of the 2nd floor. If 1” x 4” x 4’ T&G flooring is to be used, how many board feet is needed for the master bedroom. The effective width of T&G flooring boards is 3.25”. Provide at least 5% wastage allowance.
n: The area of the master bedroom is 77sqm x 0.4 = 30.8 sqm. The effective coverage of each flooring board is 3.25” x 4 feet = 156 sq.in. = 0.100645 sqm. Therefore, the number of boards needed is 30.8 sqm / 0.100645 sqm = 306.02 pcs x 1.05 = 321.3 pcs or 322 pcs. 30.8 sqm / 0.1006 sqm per board = 306 boards. Add 5% for waste: 322 pcs. Source: Fajardo, Simplified Construction Estimate (Lumber – Flooring).

q: What do you call a house with at least three different levels?
n: A split-level house has floor levels offset by about half a storey, usually three or more levels joined by short flights of stairs. Source: Ching, A Visual Dictionary of Architecture; Harris, Dictionary of Architecture and Construction.

q: One of the windows of the master bedroom will be used as an emergency exit. What should be the dimension of the opening of this window?
n: Emergency escape windows need a minimum clear opening of about 0.5 sqm, at least 510 mm wide and 610 mm high. Among the choices, 820 mm × 1.0 m satisfies these. Source: NFPA 101, Sec. 24.2.2.3.3 (Secondary Means of Escape – Windows); RA 9514 RIRR.

q: The roofed porch of the left unit has an elevation of 450mm from the sidewalk. How many entrance steps are needed?
n: This question is tricky if you don’t know the requirements for entrance steps and ramps. According to the building code, entrance steps shall have a minimum of 2 steps, min of 300mm tread width and maximum of 100 mm riser height. Since the height of the porch is given, we should consider the maximum riser height. Therefore, there should be at least 5 steps (450mm divided 5 steps to get a riser height below 100mm). Per the exam key, 5 steps keep each riser under the riser limit for a 450 mm rise. Source: 2004 Revised IRR of PD 1096 (NBCP), Rule VIII (Entrance Steps); BP 344 IRR (Stairs).
